To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SRA is a complex disease with several clinical phenotypes and immunological features.

SRA patients had higher prevalence of Staphylococcus aureus‐associated superantigens (SAg)‐specific IgE than patients with mild/moderate asthma (MMA) and healthy controls (HC), and that the presence of SAg-specific IgE in SRA patients was related to higher levels of IL-5, IL-13, and IL-17 in the sputum.
(1) SRA is associated with the presence of Staphylococcus aureus‐specific IgE, and (2) the presence of these antibodies may serve as a useful biomarker in the diagnosis of SRA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical and immunological characteristics of SRA.
the development of new, efficient methods for the determination of the concentration of the superantigen staphylococci enterotoxin C (SEC) in the environment.
the clinical and immunological features of SRA, and the role of bacterial superantigens in its pathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SRA is a heterogeneous group of patients, which may be subdivided into several subgroups, including those with high IgE and/or IgG antibodies to bacterial superantigens.
the presence of SAAS‐specific IgE is a significant risk factor for SRA, but it cannot be used as a stand‐alone diagnostic marker.
SRA is not a distinct disease entity, but a heterogeneous group of diseases with common clinical features and a variety of underlying immunological mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified an important new mechanism of severe asthma, namely, the association of S. aureus superantigen‐ specific IgE with severe asthma.
we have shown that Staph superantigen‐associated IgE is a novel marker of SRA and may be useful for the diagnosis and monitoring of this disease.
SRA patients have a distinct clinical and immunological phenotype, and this phenotype is associated with a specific pattern of IgE reactivity to bacterial superantigens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical features associated with the presence of SA‐specific IgE in SRA are different from those associated with the presence SA‐specific IgG.
the presence of IgE antibodies against Staphylococcus aureus enterotoxins is a risk factor for severe refractory asthma, which can be used to guide therapy.
the presence of Staphylococcus superantigen-specific IgE antibodies is an important factor in severe asthma.
